high_level_description: The image is a split-screen presentation during what appears to be an academic or professional lecture. On the left side of the screen, there is a slide with a beige background featuring a visual illusion known as the "Checkerboard Illusion" by Edward H. Adelson. The slide includes two checkerboards, each with a green cylinder placed on top. The checkerboards are designed to create an optical illusion where the squares appear to have different shades of gray, despite being the same color. The text on the slide reads: "But sometimes 'not seeing' is more profound.
